identity.title: Food Safety Plan for Ready-to-Eat Hummus and Bean Dips

scan.summary: This is a written food safety plan required by FDA's Preventive Controls for Human Food rule (21 CFR Part 117). It describes the company's hazard analysis, preventive controls, monitoring, corrective actions, and verification procedures for producing refrigerated ready-to-eat hummus and bean dips. The plan is prepared by a qualified individual (PCQI) and covers biological, chemical, and physical hazards in the manufacturing process.
scan.freshness_note: The plan is dated May 12, 2025, and was current as of today (September 29, 2026), making it 16 months old. The PCQI's FSPCA training is current as of March 2024, over two years old as of today. For a plan governing food safety controls, this is acceptable, but PCQI training currency should be monitored—FSPCA certificates have expiration dates that should be checked.

gaps.title: Food Defense plan missing
gaps.description: The document lacks a food defense plan addressing intentional adulteration. FSMA Preventive Controls rule requires facilities to evaluate and address the risk of intentional adulteration of food.
gaps.fix: Add a section on food defense that identifies potential vulnerabilities in the process and storage areas, and describes measures to prevent intentional adulteration. Reference 21 CFR Part 121 (Mitigation Strategies to Prevent Food Against Intentional Adulteration).
gaps.citation: 21 CFR 121 (FSMA Mitigation Strategies to Prevent Food Against Intentional Adulteration)

gaps.title: Reanalysis protocol not specified
gaps.description: The plan does not document when and how the food safety plan will be reanalyzed. FSMA requires a reanalysis of hazards and preventive controls at least every three years, or sooner if there are changes to the facility, process, ingredients, or label claims.
gaps.fix: Add a section stating that the plan will be reanalyzed at least every three years from the date of approval, or sooner if there are significant changes. Document the reanalysis schedule and the name of the responsible individual (the PCQI).

gaps.title: Recall plan missing
gaps.description: The document does not include a written recall plan. FSMA requires facilities to establish procedures for recall, including identification of products, responsible parties, and communication procedures.
gaps.fix: Add a section describing the recall plan, including how products will be identified and traced, procedures for notifying customers and distributors, and the party responsible for initiating a recall.
gaps.citation: 21 CFR 117.190 — Requirements for a food recall plan

gaps.title: Validation of preventive controls not documented
gaps.description: While the plan describes monitoring and verification activities, it does not explicitly state that the preventive controls have been validated to show they can achieve the intended risk reduction. Validation is the scientific/technical basis demonstrating that a control can reliably achieve the desired outcome.
gaps.fix: Add documentation of validation studies or citations to published data demonstrating that the cook step (212°F for 60 minutes) achieves the required log reduction for Salmonella and Listeria monocytogenes, and that the cooling parameters prevent spore-former outgrowth. Document validation of the sanitation control and allergen control procedures.

gaps.title: Supplier approval criteria not fully documented
gaps.description: The supply-chain program states that tahini and dry beans must come from approved suppliers with a third-party audit certificate and certificate of analysis, but does not document the criteria used to evaluate suppliers or the mechanism for removing a supplier from the approved list.
gaps.fix: Add detailed supplier approval criteria, including the standards for third-party audit certificates (e.g., SQF, BRC, FSSC 22000), the scope of analyses required, and the procedures for re-evaluation, suspension, or removal of suppliers from the approved list.
gaps.quote: Tahini and dry beans are received only from approved suppliers who provide a current third-party audit certificate and a certificate of analysis for each lot.

gaps.title: Allergen controls may be incomplete for sesame (tahini source)
gaps.description: The plan identifies sesame as a known allergen in tahini and controls for hummus labeling, but does not document controls to verify that bean dip formulations do not contain tahini (to prevent cross-contact in products not labeled with sesame). The hazard table states hummus requires sesame labeling, but the control strategy does not explicitly cover prevention of sesame in non-sesame bean dips.
gaps.fix: Clarify in the preventive controls section whether bean dips are formulated with or without tahini. If bean dips do not contain tahini, add a control to verify ingredient formulations and segregate bean dips from hummus products during storage and handling to prevent cross-contact. If tahini is used in some bean dips, add sesame to those labels.
gaps.quote: Contains: sesame" for all hummus items

gaps.title: Finished product testing frequency not justified
gaps.description: The plan specifies monthly testing of finished product for Listeria monocytogenes by an accredited laboratory, but does not provide scientific justification for this frequency or reference to sampling plans (such as ICMSF or FDA guidance on Listeria in RTE foods).
gaps.fix: Add documentation of the sampling plan basis, including reference to FDA's Draft Guidance on Control of Listeria monocytogenes in Ready-to-Eat Foods (January 2017) or ICMSF sampling plans. Specify the number of samples per lot or per month, the size of each sample (should be at least 25g per FDA zero-tolerance policy), and the analytical method. Explain why monthly frequency is adequate given the risk.
gaps.citation: FDA Draft Guidance on Control of Listeria monocytogenes in Ready-to-Eat Foods (January 2017)
gaps.quote: Finished product is tested for Listeria monocytogenes monthly by an accredited laboratory.

gaps.title: ATP and Listeria swab sampling sites and frequency not detailed
gaps.description: The plan states that environmental monitoring includes ATP swabs and Listeria spp. swabs, with Listeria swabs taken weekly at 10 sites in zones 1 and 2, but does not provide detailed locations of the 10 sites, descriptions of zones 1 and 2, or justification for the frequency and coverage.
gaps.fix: Add a detailed map or list of the specific 10 swab sites, including equipment contact surfaces, floors, walls, and other critical areas. Define zones 1 (food contact surfaces and immediate environment) and zone 2 (broader environment). Reference FDA or FSIS guidance on environmental monitoring and justify the sampling frequency and locations based on the risk of Listeria in the environment.
gaps.citation: FDA Draft Guidance on Control of Listeria monocytogenes in Ready-to-Eat Foods (January 2017); 21 CFR 117.165(c)
gaps.quote: Listeria spp. swabs, 10 sites weekly, zone 1 and 2

gaps.title: Environmental monitoring trending process not defined
gaps.description: Section 7 states that environmental monitoring results are trended quarterly, but the plan does not explain what action levels or thresholds trigger investigation or corrective action (e.g., increase in Listeria spp. detection rate, new sites becoming positive).
gaps.fix: Add a section describing the trend analysis methodology, including what constitutes a significant trend (e.g., increasing frequency, new positive sites, positive results in zones previously negative). Define action levels that trigger investigation or intensified corrective action.
gaps.quote: Environmental monitoring results are trended quarterly.

gaps.title: Definition of adequate cooling time in context of clostridial risk
gaps.description: The cooling control specifies cooling from 135°F to 70°F in 2 hours, then to 41°F in 4 more hours. However, the plan does not document the scientific basis or reference to published data showing that these time-temperature parameters prevent Clostridium perfringens and Bacillus cereus outgrowth in legume-based products.
gaps.fix: Add validation data or cite published studies showing that the specified cooling curve is adequate to prevent clostridial outgrowth. Reference food safety literature on thermoduric spore-former control in cooked legumes.
gaps.quote: Cool cooked beans from 135°F to 70°F within 2 hours and to 41°F within a further 4 hours in the blast chiller

gaps.title: PCQI training currency requirement not documented
gaps.description: The plan states that Dana Whitfield, the PCQI, holds a FSPCA certificate dated March 2024. However, the plan does not specify the expiration date of the FSPCA certificate or a procedure to ensure the PCQI's training remains current or is renewed before expiration.
gaps.fix: Add a statement documenting the expiration date of the PCQI's FSPCA certificate and a commitment to renew training before expiration. Include a schedule for refresher training if required.
gaps.quote: Dana Whitfield, Quality Manager, Preventive Controls Qualified Individual (PCQI certificate, FSPCA course, March 2024)

expected_missing.title: Written Food Defense Plan
expected_missing.why: FSMA Mitigation Strategies to Prevent Food Against Intentional Adulteration (21 CFR Part 121) require covered facilities to develop and implement a food defense plan identifying vulnerabilities and mitigation strategies.
expected_missing.basis: Regulatory requirement; similar facilities producing RTE foods for retail distribution are required to have a food defense plan

expected_missing.title: Product Traceability and Recall Procedures
expected_missing.why: FSMA requires a written recall plan identifying product categories, distribution channels, procedures for tracing forward and backward, and communication procedures for recalls.
expected_missing.basis: 21 CFR 117.190; standard requirement for facilities producing RTE foods for distribution beyond a single site

expected_missing.title: Validation Documentation for Preventive Controls
expected_missing.why: FDA guidance and 21 CFR 117.165(b) expect documentation showing that the facility's preventive controls (cook step, cooling, sanitation, etc.) have been validated to achieve the intended safety outcomes based on scientific data or published literature.
expected_missing.basis: 21 CFR 117.165(b) and FDA Preventive Controls Guidance; similar RTE food facilities typically maintain validation studies

expected_missing.title: HACCP or Preliminary Steps Documentation
expected_missing.why: While not explicitly required in the plan itself, FSMA documentation often includes preliminary steps such as a product description summary, process flow diagram, and identification of which preventive controls are 'critical' vs. 'supporting,' which this plan lacks in formal structure.
expected_missing.basis: FDA Preventive Controls Guidance and industry best practice for FSMA food safety plans

expected_missing.title: Supplier Approval Criteria and Records
expected_missing.why: A detailed supplier evaluation and approval SOP documenting the criteria for third-party audit certificates, frequency of re-evaluation, and procedures for suspension or removal from the approved supplier list is expected to accompany the supply-chain program section.
expected_missing.basis: 21 CFR 117.80 and FDA Preventive Controls Guidance; standard practice for facilities with external suppliers

scan.confidence_notes: High confidence in what the document states and contains. The plan is clearly written and includes the major required elements: hazard analysis, preventive controls, monitoring procedures, corrective actions, and verification activities. However, several significant gaps exist where the document does not address explicit FSMA or FDA guidance requirements, particularly: (1) food defense plan (required by 21 CFR Part 121), (2) reanalysis protocol (required by 21 CFR 117.180), (3) recall plan (required by 21 CFR 117.190), (4) validation of controls (required by 21 CFR 117.165), and (5) detailed sampling justification for Listeria testing and environmental monitoring (expected per FDA Listeria guidance). These are not gaps in the company's operations but gaps in the documentation of the plan itself. The control measures described (cooking, cooling, sanitation, allergen management, metal detection) appear sound for a ready-to-eat hummus and bean dip facility, and the monitoring and corrective action procedures are reasonable. The supply-chain program is described but lacks detail on supplier approval criteria. The allergen control strategy for sesame is adequate for hummus but may not fully address cross-contact prevention for bean dips if they are produced without tahini. Confidence is medium for the overall adequacy of the plan as submitted against FSMA full requirements, but high for the core process controls.

WILLAMETTE VALLEY FOODS, INC.
FOOD SAFETY PLAN
Ready-to-eat hummus and bean dips
Salem Plant, 1850 Fairgrounds Road NE, Salem, Oregon 97301
Effective date: May 12, 2025
Prepared by: Dana Whitfield, Quality Manager, Preventive Controls Qualified Individual
(PCQI certificate, FSPCA course, March 2024)
Approved by: Plant Manager
1. Facility and product description
Willamette Valley Foods produces refrigerated ready-to-eat hummus and bean dips in 8-ounce and 16-
ounce sealed plastic tubs for retail sale in Oregon, Washington and Idaho. The Salem plant operates one
shift, five days a week, with 28 production employees. Products are made from cooked chickpeas or black
beans, tahini, lemon juice, garlic, olive oil, salt and spices, blended, filled, sealed, coded and held
refrigerated at or below 41°F. Shelf life is 45 days refrigerated. Products are labeled with the allergen
statement "Contains: sesame" for all hummus items.
2. Process flow
Receiving of dry beans, tahini and other ingredients → dry storage or refrigerated storage → soaking and
cooking of beans (kettle, 212°F, 60 minutes minimum) → cooling in the blast chiller → blending with
other ingredients → filling and sealing → date coding → metal detection → refrigerated storage →
shipping.

the day, followed by full washdown the next non-sesame product
Metal Metal detection of every sealed tub Process Reject at 2.0 mm ferrous, 2.5 mm non-
ferrous, 3.0 mm stainless test pieces
5. Monitoring
The kettle operator records the internal temperature and the time at the start and end of each cook batch
on the cook log. The blast chiller operator records the temperature at 2 hours and at 6 hours on the cooling
log. The sanitation lead records the ATP swab result before each start-up. The line lead runs the three
metal test pieces through the detector at start-up, every two hours, and at the end of the run, and records
the result. The quality technician reviews every label lot against the formulation sheet at receipt and signs
the label log.
6. Corrective actions
If a cook batch does not reach 212°F for 60 minutes, the batch is re-cooked to the critical limit or
discarded, and the cause is recorded. If cooling exceeds the time limits, the batch is discarded. If an ATP
swab fails, the surface is re-cleaned and re-swabbed before production starts. If a Listeria spp. swab is
positive, the site is cleaned and re-swabbed, adjacent sites are added, and product made on that line since
the last negative swab is held pending investigation. If the metal detector fails a test piece, all product
since the last passing test is re-run through the detector. If a label does not match the formulation, the lot
is quarantined and not used. All corrective actions are recorded on the corrective action log and reviewed
by the PCQI within seven days.
7. Verification
The PCQI reviews the cook, cooling, sanitation, allergen and metal detection records within seven
working days of their creation. Probe thermometers are calibrated in ice water and boiling water weekly,
and the metal detector is serviced by the manufacturer annually. Finished product is tested for Listeria
monocytogenes monthly by an accredited laboratory. Environmental monitoring results are trended
quarterly.
8. Supply-chain program
Tahini and dry beans are received only from approved suppliers who provide a current third-party audit
certificate and a certificate of analysis for each lot. The approved supplier list is maintained by the quality
manager.
9. Records
All records named in this plan are kept at the Salem plant for at least two years from the date of the record
and are available to FDA and the Oregon Department of Agriculture on request. Records are reviewed and
signed by the PCQI as described in section 7.
10. Training
All production employees receive food hygiene training at hire and annually. The PCQI holds a current
FSPCA certificate. Sanitation and line leads are trained on the monitoring procedures in this plan.
